Familywise error correction for voxelwise GLMs in fmri.pipeline

Michael Hallquist

Source: vignettes/fwe.Rmd
fwe.Rmd

The whole-brain walkthrough produces a group z-statistic map for the participant-level faces-minus-houses contrast. This guide corrects that map for the many spatial tests inside its model mask. You can register pTFCE when specifying the GLM, run it after estimation, or use the standalone AFNI tools to make cluster-level inferences.

Workflow Inputs What to inspect
pTFCE, automatically after L3 or from a saved analysis Completed FSL L3 z-statistic, model mask, and FEAT smoothness file Enhanced statistic, FWE threshold table, and a signed thresholded image for each requested alpha
AFNI spatial ACF and 3dClustSim First-level residuals and corresponding masks, group statistic, and group search mask Cluster extent threshold, surviving cluster table, and integer cluster labels
AFNI residual sign randomization and 3dClustSim Residual maps from an appropriate group test and its search mask Cluster thresholds calibrated from randomized group residuals

Specify the search region, alpha, and sidedness before looking at the result. A whole-brain correction covers the voxels in the model mask. Each correction controls the spatial family for one map. If you make a single claim across several contrasts, models, or visits, account for those additional tests in the analysis plan. pTFCE uses spatial support to enhance the statistic without a single cluster-forming threshold. AFNI extent correction uses a specified voxelwise threshold and makes an inference about the extent of the resulting clusters. Report the method that produced the result. Spisák et al. (2019), Cox et al. (2017)

Correct a completed group analysis

The declarative interface uses the completed gpa from the batch cache. The package currently supports planned and automatic pTFCE for FSL L3. Install fmri.pipeline and the HallquistLab pTFCE fork (version 0.4.0 or later) on the host that runs correction. The tested revision is pinned in the package’s DESCRIPTION under Remotes. Verify that the R interpreter used by your job can load both packages.

Specify the target and search region

Select the map by session, model, and contrast at each level. Here the two higher-level ~ 1 models carry the lower-level comparison forward. The statistical question is the group mean face-minus-house effect.

library(fmri.pipeline)

spec <- fwe_spec(
  name = "facehouse_ptfce",
  method = "ptfce",
  targets = list(
    session = 1L,
    l1_model = "facehouse",
    l1_cope_name = "faces_minus_houses",
    l2_model = "run_average", l2_cope_name = "EV_Intercept",
    l3_model = "group_mean", l3_cope_name = "EV_Intercept"
  ),
  correction_mask = "model",
  fwe_alpha = c(0.05, 0.01),
  two_sided = TRUE,
  write_threshold_images = TRUE
)
spec

With two_sided = TRUE, pTFCE enhances both tails on a shared threshold grid and uses half of the requested alpha per tail. Positive surviving values favor faces in this example and negative values favor houses. Use two_sided = FALSE for a pre-specified positive-tail test. A planned test in the opposite direction can use an explicitly reversed contrast.

For a pre-specified small-volume correction, set correction_mask to one nonempty binary NIfTI that is inside and aligned with each target’s model mask. pTFCE reuses the model smoothness estimate and recalculates the search volume and number of resels for the smaller region. Report this as a small-volume result. Atlas masks used to summarize beta estimates can have multiple labels, whereas the correction mask is binary.

Keep the correction specification with the analysis script. A saved YAML specification can be compiled again after refitting.

write_fwe_spec(spec, "config/facehouse_ptfce.yaml")
spec <- read_fwe_spec("config/facehouse_ptfce.yaml")

Inspect the plan and run it

Planning resolves the named contrasts to files. The default output directory is <analysis>/fwe/<spec name>/. Planning itself creates no files and runs no jobs.

fwe_plan <- plan_fwe_correction(gpa, spec, refresh_status = TRUE)
fwe_plan

fwe_plan$targets[, c("target_id", "session", "l1_cope_name", "l3_cope_name")]
fwe_plan$tasks[, c(
  "task_id", "target_id", "zstat_file",
  "correction_mask_file", "smoothness_file", "status"
)]
fwe_plan$artifacts[, c("task_id", "artifact_role", "fwe_alpha", "artifact_file")]
stopifnot(nrow(fwe_plan$tasks) == 1L)

Expect one task for the face/house example. For a zero-match error, look up the maps with lookup_feat_outputs(gpa, level = 3L)$l3 and compare the semantic labels and session to spec$targets. If you expect the results but some files are still missing, use require_inputs = FALSE on the plan to inspect the status and missing_inputs columns. A blocked task cannot run until its inputs are available.

preview <- run_fwe_plan(fwe_plan, dry_run = TRUE)
preview$execution[, c("task_id", "execution_status", "command")]

write_fwe_plan(fwe_plan, "config/facehouse_ptfce_plan.rds")

fwe_run <- run_fwe_plan(fwe_plan, scheduler = "local")

The dry run lets you check exact files and commands before starting. Local execution is synchronous. For batch processing, call run_fwe_plan() with scheduler = "slurm" or "torque" and set resources for the correction jobs, such as memgb_per_command and time_per_command. Collect after the jobs finish. In a new R session, read_fwe_plan() reloads the saved plan.

Collect and interpret the results 

fwe_result <- collect_fwe_results(fwe_run, require_complete = TRUE)

thresholds <- fwe_result_artifacts(fwe_result, artifact_role = "threshold_table")
stopifnot(nrow(thresholds) == 1L)
readr::read_csv(thresholds$artifact_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

surviving <- fwe_result_artifacts(
  fwe_result,
  artifact_role = "thresholded_statistic",
  fwe_alpha = 0.05
)
surviving[, c("target_id", "l1_cope_name", "l3_cope_name",
              "artifact_file", "can_use_as_mask")]

The threshold table records the enhanced statistic cutoff (z_ptfce), requested FWE alpha (p_value), search volume in voxels, and number of surviving voxels. A row with significant_voxels = 0 is a valid result. The thresholded image preserves the sign of surviving values and is zero elsewhere. Use the beta extraction guide to turn its support into an ROI mask and extract unthresholded COPEs. The enhanced values in that image describe inference, while COPEs carry the effect size.

Collecting writes manifest/artifacts.csv and manifest/result.rds under the correction output directory. The manifest preserves target labels, source files, and threshold settings. To review a previously saved result, call collect_fwe_results() on its directory or result RDS.

If collection fails, run collect_fwe_results(fwe_run, require_complete = FALSE) and inspect the manifest’s artifact_status, task_status, and log_file columns. If run_fwe_plan() stopped before returning a run object, collect from the plan’s output directory when a result snapshot exists there. You can also use stop_on_error = FALSE to retain task statuses when rerunning. Check that all inputs are readable and that the worker can load pTFCE. Verified completion requires matching input content and settings, a successful worker receipt, and validated output files. Files from older runs without a receipt are unverified. A rerun skips verified tasks by default and recomputes stale or incomplete outputs. Use force = TRUE to rerun verified tasks as well.

Run pTFCE automatically after L3

To put correction in the original pipeline submission, add the following inference block to the existing group_mean model in facehouse.yaml. The interactive model builder also offers group inference for compatible models.

    inference:
      method: ptfce
      targets:
        l1_cope_name: faces_minus_houses
      correction_mask: model
      fwe_alpha: [0.05, 0.01]
      two_sided: true
      compute:
        scheduler: inherit

Rebuild L3 from the edited specification. Alternatively, attach the spec created above using gpa$l3_models$models$group_mean$inference <- spec. export_glm_config() preserves declarative inference settings.

gpa <- build_l3_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "facehouse.yaml")

run_glm_pipeline(
  gpa, l1_model_names = "facehouse",
  l2_model_names = "run_average", l3_model_names = "group_mean"
)

The pipeline collects the completed fit metadata and then runs a separate run_fwe stage. Check the group fit and the correction status in the diagnosis guide. Set run_fwe = FALSE in run_glm_pipeline() to skip correction for one submission.

If only correction needs to run again, reload the completed batch’s gpa and use the correction-only entry point. It requires the model’s inference settings or a declarative specification configured with build_fwe_correction().

gpa <- run_fwe_correction(gpa, l3_model_names = "group_mean")

# For scheduler execution, wait until the submitted correction jobs finish.
gpa <- refresh_fwe_correction(gpa, require_complete = TRUE)
gpa$fwe_status
names(gpa$fwe_runs)

For a standalone FEAT directory without a pipeline configuration, supply the completed .gfeat directly. Choose zstat_numbers after checking the contrast names in FEAT.

ptfce <- ptfce_spec$new(
  gfeat_dir = group_map$analysis_dir,
  zstat_numbers = group_map$l3_cope_number,
  fwe_p = c(0.05, 0.01),
  two_sided = TRUE
)
ptfce$run()

The installed ptfce_zstat.R script accepts a FEAT group directory or an individual z-statistic and its mask and smoothness inputs. Run it with --help to see both forms.

Apply cluster thresholds with AFNI

These standalone helpers run AFNI commands and do not require an fwe_spec. For the ACF route, estimate the spatial autocorrelation from first-level GLM residuals. Then simulate fields with that spatial structure to derive cluster extent thresholds for the group search volume. The assumptions and performance depend on the design and spatial noise properties. Cox et al. (2017)

Estimate ACF from the contributing runs

Start with the group map and mask selected in the whole-brain walkthrough. The example below assumes all participants and both of their runs contributed. If any runs were excluded or a group fit used a subset, first restrict run_maps to the actual contributors. Pair each run’s residual time series with the mask from that same fit.

run_maps <- lookup_feat_outputs(
  gpa, level = 1L, what = "cope", refresh_status = TRUE
)$l1 |>
  dplyr::filter(
    l1_model == "facehouse", l1_cope_name == "faces_minus_houses",
    session == 1L, analysis_status == "complete", image_exists
  )

run_dirs <- unique(run_maps$image_feat_dir)
residuals <- file.path(run_dirs, "stats", "res4d.nii.gz")
run_masks <- file.path(run_dirs, "mask.nii.gz")
stopifnot(length(run_dirs) > 0L, all(file.exists(c(residuals, run_masks))))

acf_dir <- file.path(gpa$output_directory, "fwe", "facehouse_acf")
dir.create(acf_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

run_acf <- vapply(seq_along(residuals), function(i) {
  fwhmx <- afni_3dfwhmx$new(
    input_file = residuals[i], mask_file = run_masks[i]
  )
  fwhmx$run()
  stopifnot(fwhmx$is_complete())
  setNames(fwhmx$get_acf_params()[1:3], c("a", "b", "c"))
}, FUN.VALUE = numeric(3))

acf_summary <- data.frame(residuals, t(run_acf))
acf_summary
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(run_acf)),
  all(run_acf["a", ] >= 0 & run_acf["a", ] <= 1),
  all(run_acf[c("b", "c"), ] > 0)
)

sim <- afni_3dclustsim$new(
  fwhmx_input_files = residuals,
  fwhmx_mask_files = run_masks,
  clustsim_mask = group_mask,
  out_dir = acf_dir,
  prefix = "facehouse_acf",
  pthr = 0.001, athr = 0.05,
  scheduler = "local", ncpus = 1L, seed = 42L
)
sim$submit()
sim$is_complete()

Inspect the per-run ACF estimates before pooling them. 3dFWHMx saves its outputs alongside each residual file. afni_3dclustsim reads those estimates and takes the arithmetic mean of the three parameters across runs. If the checks fail, review the affected residuals, masks, and 3dFWHMx output before pooling. If the fit did not retain residuals, obtain them from the matching GLM before using this route. Wait until sim$is_complete() returns TRUE before applying the threshold.

Apply and record the matching threshold

This example uses voxelwise p = 0.001, clusterwise alpha 0.05, and NN1 (face adjacency). AFNI’s bi-sided setting finds positive and negative clusters separately using a two-tail threshold. Use the same search volume, sidedness, connectivity, and voxelwise p value as in the selected simulation row. AFNI 3dClustSim documentation

stopifnot(sim$is_complete())
sim$get_clustsim_df() |>
  dplyr::filter(nn == 1L, sided == "bi", pthr == 0.001, athr == 0.05)

cobj <- sim$apply_clustsim(
  statistic_nifti = group_map$image_file,
  NN = 1L, sided = "bi", pthr = 0.001, athr = 0.05,
  voxelwise_stat = list(stat_type = "z"),
  output_cluster_mask = TRUE,
  output_thresholded_image = TRUE,
  add_whereami = FALSE
)
cobj$get_clust_df()
cobj$get_outputs()

Report the cluster-level threshold, observed extent, and location for surviving clusters. Cluster-extent inference does not establish a voxelwise claim for each voxel in a cluster. The integer cluster_map is the input for extracting one effect per cluster.

Use residual sign randomization for a suitable group test

The residuals_file mode of afni_3dclustsim generates null statistic maps with 3dttest++ and passes them to 3dClustSim. Use it when independent, sign-exchangeable group residuals represent the intended one-sample test. This wrapper’s residual sign flips do not model repeated measures, group-label exchange, or arbitrary covariate designs. Use a null-generation method justified for your group design. Supply a group-level 4D residual image with one volume per observation and its matching 3D search mask.

# Paths from the one-sample analysis being corrected
residual_dir <- file.path(gpa$output_directory, "fwe", "one_sample_residuals")
dir.create(residual_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

sim <- afni_3dclustsim$new(
  residuals_file = "/study/one_sample/group_residuals.nii.gz",
  residuals_mask_file = "/study/one_sample/group_mask.nii.gz",
  residuals_njobs = 30L,
  out_dir = residual_dir,
  prefix = "one_sample",
  scheduler = "slurm"
)
sim$submit()

After completion, inspect sim$get_clustsim_df() and apply the matching threshold to the statistic from that one-sample analysis. Keep the simulation settings, mask, and statistic together when recording the result.
